title: 瑤池金母消愆解罪報恩功德懺

pages.subtitle: The title, five verses, the Holy Name and the petition

lines.head: Title
lines.zh: 瑤池金母消愆解罪報恩功德懺
lines.py: yáo chí jīn mǔ xiāo qiān jiě zuì bào ēn gōng dé chàn
tr: The Repentance of the Golden Mother of the Jasper Pool — for dissolving transgressions, releasing sins, and repaying grace through merit and virtue.

lines.head: Verse 1
lines.zh: 瑤池金母降旨來。引導靈脈收圓臺。
lines.py: yáo chí jīn mǔ jiàng zhǐ lái yǐn dǎo líng mài shōu yuán tái
tr: The Golden Mother of the Jasper Pool sends down her decree and comes.
She guides the spirit-lineage to the Terrace of the Final Ingathering.

lines.head: Verse 2
lines.zh: 靈元復旨應天界。龍子鳳兒智慧開。
lines.py: líng yuán fù zhǐ yìng tiān jiè lóng zǐ fèng ér zhì huì kāi
tr: The spirit-origin reports back on the decree and answers to the heavenly realm.
The dragon-sons and phoenix-children have their wisdom opened.

lines.head: Verse 3
lines.zh: 累世因果緣主宰。教化人心離塵埃。
lines.py: lěi shì yīn guǒ yuán zhǔ zǎi jiào huà rén xīn lí chén āi
tr: Over the karma and affinities of accumulated lifetimes, she presides.
She teaches and transforms the human heart, that it may leave the dust.

lines.head: Verse 4
lines.zh: 誦唸懺文轉法台。不迷五濁六塵界。
lines.py: sòng niàn chàn wén zhuǎn fǎ tái bù mí wǔ zhuó liù chén jiè
tr: Reciting and chanting the repentance text turns the Dharma-terrace.
Then one is not lost in the realm of the Five Turbidities and Six Dusts.

lines.head: Verse 5
lines.zh: 金丹大道傳法開。傳授心法返瑤台。
lines.py: jīn dān dà dào chuán fǎ kāi chuán shòu xīn fǎ fǎn yáo tái
tr: The Great Way of the Golden Elixir opens its transmission.
The heart-method is conferred, and one returns to the Jasper Terrace.

lines.head: Holy Name — first occurrence
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wújí Yáochí Dàshèng Xīwáng Jīnmǔ Dàtiānzūn

lines.head: Petition
lines.zh: 今日齋主發虔誠。禮拜懺悔赦罪刑。
lines.py: jīn rì zhāi zhǔ fā qián chéng lǐ bài chàn huǐ shè zuì xíng
tr: Today the rite's sponsor gives rise to reverent sincerity.
Bowing and repenting — may the penalty of sin be pardoned.

lines.head: Closing couplet
lines.zh: 消愆解罪福頻頻。慈悲普救十方人。
lines.py: xiāo qiān jiě zuì fú pín pín cí bēi pǔ jiù shí fāng rén
tr: Transgressions dissolved, sins released — blessings come again and again.
In compassion she universally saves the people of the ten directions.

pages.subtitle: The first and second debts: heaven and earth, sun and moon

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wújí Yáochí Dàshèng Xīwáng Jīnmǔ Dàtiānzūn

lines.head: Verse 1
lines.zh: 誦經有請降來臨。災消病減除罪名。
lines.py: sòng jīng yǒu qǐng jiàng lái lín zāi xiāo bìng jiǎn chú zuì míng
tr: Scripture is recited, and with reverence she is invited to descend and draw near.
Calamity dissolves, sickness lessens, the charge of sin is struck from the record.

lines.head: Verse 2
lines.zh: 一報天地蓋載恩。天覆地載豈非輕。
lines.py: yī bào tiān dì gài zài ēn tiān fù dì zài qǐ fēi qīng
tr: The first debt repaid: the grace of heaven's covering and earth's bearing.
Heaven covers, earth carries — how could this be counted a small thing?

lines.head: Verse 3
lines.zh: 天降甘露潤生靈。地發萬物養群生。
lines.py: tiān jiàng gān lù rùn shēng líng dì fā wàn wù yǎng qún shēng
tr: Heaven sends down sweet dew and moistens the living souls.
Earth puts forth the ten thousand things and nourishes the multitude.

lines.head: Verse 4
lines.zh: 持齋受戒明禮義。報答天地蓋載恩。
lines.py: chí zhāi shòu jiè míng lǐ yì bào dá tiān dì gài zài ēn
tr: Keep the fast, receive the precepts, understand propriety and rightness.
Thus repay the grace of heaven's covering and earth's bearing.

lines.head: Verse 5
lines.zh: 二報日月照靈恩。日月普照大乾坤。
lines.py: èr bào rì yuè zhào líng ēn rì yuè pǔ zhào dà qián kūn
tr: The second debt repaid: the grace of sun and moon illumining the spirit.
Sun and moon shine everywhere upon the great Qian and Kun.

pages.subtitle: The second and third debts: sun and moon, sovereign and soil

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wújí Yáochí Dàshèng Xīwáng Jīnmǔ Dàtiānzūn

lines.head: Verse 1 — illustration of the second debt
lines.zh: 東出西沒運轉行。周而復始放光明。
lines.py: dōng chū xī mò yùn zhuǎn xíng zhōu ér fù shǐ fàng guāng míng
tr: Rising in the east, sinking in the west, they wheel and turn and travel on.
The circuit completes and begins again, pouring out light.

lines.head: Verse 2 — discharge of the second debt
lines.zh: 持齋受戒明心性。報答日月照靈恩。
lines.py: chí zhāi shòu jiè míng xīn xìng bào dá rì yuè zhào líng ēn
tr: Keep the fast, receive the precepts, illuminate the heart-nature.
Thus repay the grace of sun and moon illumining the spirit.

lines.head: Verse 3 — naming of the third debt
lines.zh: 三報皇王水土恩。皇王水土養黎民。
lines.py: sān bào huáng wáng shuǐ tǔ ēn huáng wáng shuǐ tǔ yǎng lí mín
tr: The third debt repaid: the grace of the sovereign and of water and soil.
Sovereign, water and soil nourish the common people.

lines.head: Verse 4 — illustration of the third debt
lines.zh: 君王有道民安樂。八方寧靜好修行。
lines.py: jūn wáng yǒu dào mín ān lè bā fāng níng jìng hǎo xiū xíng
tr: When the ruler possesses the Way, the people are at peace and glad.
The eight directions are quiet and still — good for cultivation.

lines.head: Verse 5 — discharge of the third debt
lines.zh: 持齋受戒行正道。報答皇王水土恩。
lines.py: chí zhāi shòu jiè xíng zhèng dào bào dá huáng wáng shuǐ tǔ ēn
tr: Keep the fast, receive the precepts, walk the upright path.
Thus repay the grace of the sovereign and of water and soil.

pages.subtitle: The fourth debt (parents) and the opening of the fifth (the teacher)

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wújí Yáochí Dàshèng Xīwáng Jīnmǔ Dàtiānzūn

lines.head: Verse 1 — naming of the fourth debt
lines.zh: 四報爺娘養育恩。爺娘恩情大海深。
lines.py: sì bào yé niáng yǎng yù ēn yé niáng ēn qíng dà hǎi shēn
tr: The fourth debt repaid: the grace of father and mother who raised us.
The kindness of father and mother is deep as the great sea.

lines.head: Verse 2 — conduct for the fourth debt
lines.zh: 為人子女順道行。行至處處皆成蔭。
lines.py: wéi rén zǐ nǚ shùn dào xíng xíng zhì chù chù jiē chéng yìn
tr: As sons and daughters, walk in accord with the Way.
Wherever that walking reaches, every place becomes shade.

lines.head: Verse 3 — closing of the fourth debt
lines.zh: 父是天來母是地。敬顧父母鬼神欽。
lines.py: fù shì tiān lái mǔ shì dì jìng gù fù mǔ guǐ shén qīn
tr: Father is heaven, mother is earth.
Revere and care for your father and mother, and the unseen powers will honour you.

lines.head: Verse 4 — naming of the fifth debt
lines.zh: 五報聖尊傳法恩。真佛密法渡眾生。
lines.py: wǔ bào shèng zūn chuán fǎ ēn zhēn fó mì fǎ dù zhòng shēng
tr: The fifth debt repaid: the grace of the Holy Honoured One who transmits the Dharma.
The true Buddha's hidden Dharma ferries all beings across.

lines.head: Verse 5 — illustration of the fifth debt
lines.zh: 廣傳妙理利陽冥。宿業消除福慧增。
lines.py: guǎng chuán miào lǐ lì yáng míng sù yè xiāo chú fú huì zēng
tr: The wondrous principle is spread widely, benefiting the living and the dead.
Karma from former lives dissolves, and blessing and wisdom increase.

pages.subtitle: The teacher, the Golden Mother, and the opening of the seventh debt

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wújí Yáochí Dàshèng Xīwáng Jīnmǔ Dàtiānzūn

lines.head: Verse 1 — closing of the fifth debt
lines.zh: 傳法之恩難酬報。時刻敬師傳法恩。
lines.py: chuán fǎ zhī ēn nán chóu bào shí kè jìng shī chuán fǎ ēn
tr: The grace of the Dharma's transmission is hard to repay.
At every moment, revere the teacher's grace of transmission.

lines.head: Verse 2 — naming of the sixth debt
lines.zh: 六報瑤池金母恩。消劫救世收圓心。
lines.py: liù bào yáo chí jīn mǔ ēn xiāo jié jiù shì shōu yuán xīn
tr: The sixth debt repaid: the grace of the Golden Mother of the Jasper Pool.
Hers is the heart that dissolves the kalpa's calamity, saves the world, and gathers all home.

lines.head: Verse 3 — conduct for the sixth debt
lines.zh: 引進勸化挽迷津。仁義禮智證成尊。
lines.py: yǐn jìn quàn huà wǎn mí jīn rén yì lǐ zhì zhèng chéng zūn
tr: Bring others in, exhort and transform them, pull them back from the ford where they have lost their way.
Through humaneness, rightness, propriety and wisdom, realise yourself and become an Honoured One.

lines.head: Verse 4 — closing of the sixth debt
lines.zh: 道德廉恥明教理。千辛萬苦渡原兒。
lines.py: dào dé lián chǐ míng jiào lǐ qiān xīn wàn kǔ dù yuán ér
tr: In the Way and virtue, integrity and shame, understand the principles of the teaching.
Through a thousand hardships and ten thousand bitternesses, ferry the original children across.

lines.head: Verse 5 — naming of the seventh debt
lines.zh: 七報本尊護法恩。若無尊護善難行。
lines.py: qī bào běn zūn hù fǎ ēn ruò wú zūn hù shàn nán xíng
tr: The seventh debt repaid: the grace of the principal Honoured One who protects the Dharma.
Without the Honoured One's protection, goodness is hard to carry out.

pages.subtitle: The protector, the good friends, and the return to the Jasper Pool

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wújí Yáochí Dàshèng Xīwáng Jīnmǔ Dàtiānzūn

lines.head: Verse 1 — illustration of the seventh debt
lines.zh: 降魔除妖滅邪穢。成就菩提護跟隨。
lines.py: xiáng mó chú yāo miè xié huì chéng jiù pú tí hù gēn suí
tr: They subdue demons, drive out goblins, and extinguish what is crooked and defiled.
Until awakening is accomplished, their protection follows close behind.

lines.head: Verse 2 — closing of the seventh debt
lines.zh: 行者善人敬尊護。神超天外功德存。
lines.py: xíng zhě shàn rén jìng zūn hù shén chāo tiān wài gōng dé cún
tr: Practitioners and good people, revere the Honoured One's protection.
The spirit rises beyond the heavens, and its merit endures.

lines.head: Verse 3 — naming of the eighth debt
lines.zh: 八報八方善智恩。明辨是非善惡分。
lines.py: bā bào bā fāng shàn zhì ēn míng biàn shì fēi shàn è fēn
tr: The eighth debt repaid: the grace of the good and wise in all eight directions.
Through them we clearly tell right from wrong, and set good apart from evil.

lines.head: Verse 4 — gathering the graces
lines.zh: 師恩母恩善智恩。相施相法出苦輪。
lines.py: shī ēn mǔ ēn shàn zhì ēn xiāng shī xiāng fǎ chū kǔ lún
tr: The teacher's grace, the Mother's grace, the grace of the good and wise.
Giving to one another, sharing the Dharma with one another, we leave the wheel of suffering.

lines.head: Verse 5 — the return home
lines.zh: 普勸原靈歸正道。一同齊歸瑤池境。
lines.py: pǔ quàn yuán líng guī zhèng dào yī tóng qí guī yáo chí jìng
tr: Urge all the original souls, everywhere, to return to the upright path.
Together, all as one, return to the realm of the Jasper Pool.

pages.subtitle: The ninth debt (the ancestors) and the tenth (the sages of every teaching)

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn

lines.head: Verse 1 — naming of the ninth debt
lines.zh: 九報九玄七祖恩。家家大同共宗親。
lines.py: jiǔ bào jiǔ xuán qī zǔ ēn jiā jiā dà tóng gòng zōng qīn
tr: The ninth debt repaid: the grace of the ancestors, every generation behind us.
Every household becomes one great family, sharing one lineage of kin.

lines.head: Verse 2 — conduct for the ninth debt
lines.zh: 若無前人無後生。光耀宗族善舉行。
lines.py: ruò wú qián rén wú hòu shēng guāng yào zōng zú shàn jǔ xíng
tr: If there were no one before us, there would be no one born after.
Bring honour to the clan by carrying out good deeds.

lines.head: Verse 3 — closing of the ninth debt
lines.zh: 一子持齋萬佛喜。九玄七祖盡超昇。
lines.py: yī zǐ chí zhāi wàn fó xǐ jiǔ xuán qī zǔ jìn chāo shēng
tr: When one child keeps the fast, ten thousand Buddhas rejoice.
And the ancestors, every generation behind, all rise beyond.

lines.head: Verse 4 — naming of the tenth debt
lines.zh: 十報萬教聖賢恩。各留經卷渡群生。
lines.py: shí bào wàn jiào shèng xián ēn gè liú jīng juàn dù qún shēng
tr: The tenth debt repaid: the grace of the sages and worthies of all the ten thousand teachings.
Each left behind scriptures to ferry the multitude across.

lines.head: Verse 5 — why the sages laboured
lines.zh: 費盡口舌萬般辛。只為娑婆原靈苦。
lines.py: fèi jìn kǒu shé wàn bān xīn zhǐ wèi suō pó yuán líng kǔ
tr: They wore out their mouths and tongues, through every kind of hardship,
only because the original souls suffer in the Sahā world.

pages.subtitle: What every scripture teaches, and the thousand graces repaid together

lines.head: Holy Name — occurrence 1
lines.zh: 無極瑤池大聖西王金母大天尊
lines.py: wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn
tr: Wú jí yáo chí dà shèng xī wáng jīn mǔ dà tiān zūn

lines.head: Verse 1 — closing of the tenth debt
lines.zh: 萬教經書言何事。皆因調和一點心。
lines.py: wàn jiào jīng shū yán hé shì jiē yīn tiáo hé yī diǎn xīn
tr: What do the scriptures of all the ten thousand teachings speak about?
All of them are about bringing one point of the heart into harmony.

lines.head: Verse 2 — all the graces repaid: the household
lines.zh: 千恩萬德皆總報。庇祐齋主家道興。
lines.py: qiān ēn wàn dé jiē zǒng bào bì yòu zhāi zhǔ jiā dào xīng
tr: The thousand graces and ten thousand kindnesses, all repaid together.
May the sponsor be sheltered and blessed, and the household flourish.

lines.head: Verse 3 — all the graces repaid: the assembly
lines.zh: 千恩萬德皆總報。庇祐合眾平安寧。
lines.py: qiān ēn wàn dé jiē zǒng bào bì yòu hé zhòng píng ān níng
tr: The thousand graces and ten thousand kindnesses, all repaid together.
May the whole assembly be sheltered and blessed, in peace and tranquillity.

lines.head: Verse 4 — all the graces repaid: the neighbours
lines.zh: 千恩萬德皆總報。庇祐鄰里永無災。
lines.py: qiān ēn wàn dé jiē zǒng bào bì yòu lín lǐ yǒng wú zāi
tr: The thousand graces and ten thousand kindnesses, all repaid together.
May the neighbours be sheltered and blessed, forever free of calamity.

lines.head: Verse 5 — all the graces repaid: blessing and wisdom
lines.zh: 千恩萬德皆總報。庇祐齋主福慧增。
lines.py: qiān ēn wàn dé jiē zǒng bào bì yòu zhāi zhǔ fú huì zēng
tr: The thousand graces and ten thousand kindnesses, all repaid together.
May the sponsor be sheltered and blessed, with merit and wisdom increasing.

沒.long: sink, go under (read mò, not méi)

劫.long: kalpa; the calamity at a world-age's end

sovereign and land, taken as one debt
the productive ground one belongs to
the common people, the dark-haired multitude

loving kindness, the warmth of a favour

靈.note: 靈 — rain 雨 over three mouths 口口口 over the shaman 巫. Rain called down by voices. The whole cosmology of this text sits in one glyph. Keep the three 口 small and even; that row is where it usually collapses.

懺.note: 懺 (20 strokes) — 忄 plus 韱. The heart-radical on the left is the doctrine: repentance is a heart-act, not a mouth-act. Give 忄 a full third of the width or the right side crushes it.

愆.note: 愆 (13 strokes) — 衍 over 心. A fault that flows out from the heart. Note it sits above 心 while 懺 sits beside it — two different relations to the heart, drawn differently.

鳳.note: 鳳 — 几 enclosing 鳥. Easy to crowd the bird; set the enclosure wide first, then fit 鳥 inside.

齋.note: 齋 — a tall, symmetrical character. Find the vertical centre line before the first stroke.
齋 — appears again from page 1 (齋主 → 持齋). Same tall symmetry, same advice: find the vertical centre before the first stroke.
齋 — third appearance (齋主, 持齋, 持齋). Same advice each time: find the vertical centre line before the first stroke. By now your hand should be starting to know it.

臺.note: 臺 vs 台 — the sheet uses full 臺 in 收圓臺 but short 台 in 轉法台 and 返瑤台. Both correct on the same page. Don't "fix" either.

台.note: 臺 vs 台 — the sheet uses full 臺 in 收圓臺 but short 台 in 轉法台 and 返瑤台. Both correct on the same page. Don't "fix" either.

德.note: 德 — the Taiwan standard keeps the short horizontal 一 above 心. It is there on your sheet. Trace it.
德 dé "virtue, kindness" — 彳 (chì, step) beside 惪 (the upright heart). Appears four times on this page; the Taiwan form keeps the short horizontal above 心.

露.note: 露 — rain 雨 on top again, now over 路 (road). Dew is rain that has taken the road down. You met 雨 in 靈 on page 1; the same weather-radical, a different descent. Keep the 雨 roof wide and flat.

覆.note: 覆 — 襾 (a cover) over 復. Note you already know 復 from 復旨 on page 1. Here it is buried under a lid, which is exactly what the character means.

乾.note: 乾 — the left side is 倝, the right is 乞. Ten strokes crowded into a narrow half. Draw the left column first and commit to its width; most failures are a left side that expands and leaves 乞 homeless.

坤.note: 坤 — by contrast, wide and calm: 土 plus 申. Qian is dense, Kun is open. The two characters look like what they mean. Write them next to each other once and see it.

萬.note: 萬 — 艹 over 禺. The lower hooks want to sprawl. Anchor the final ㇈ at the cell's baseline.

群.note: 群 — 君 beside 羊, the sheep giving the sense: a flock. Watch that 羊's three horizontals stay parallel and shorten as they rise.

沒.note: 沒 — 氵 plus 𠬛. Read mò here (to sink), not méi. The water radical is doing real work: this is the character for going under. Keep the three water strokes light and rising so the right side can drop.

復.note: 復 — you now know it from 復旨 (page 1) and have met its cousin 覆 (page 2). Here it is bare: 彳 plus 复. Compare the three on one line of scrap paper — 復, 覆, and the 彳 of 行 — and the family resemblance sorts itself out.

黎.note: 黎 — the top is 黍 (millet) compressed, the bottom 水 flattened. Twelve strokes that want more room than the cell gives. Start narrow at the top, or the final water strokes have nowhere to go.

寧.note: 寧 — a four-storey stack: 宀 / 心 / 皿 / 丁. The commonest failure is a roof too small for what it shelters. Draw 宀 generously first.

靜.note: 靜 — 青 beside 爭, both tall and both busy. Split the cell exactly in half and resist letting 青 take more.

樂.note: 樂 — symmetrical and top-heavy. Find the central 白 first, hang 幺 either side, then the 木 beneath takes the weight. Written well it looks like a bell-frame, which is what it originally depicted.

爺.note: 爺 — 父 on top, 耶 beneath. Father sitting over the rest of the word. Keep 父 broad and low like a roof; the lower part is tall and narrow and wants to push up into it.

蔭.note: 蔭 — 艹 over 陰. Grass over shadow — and 陰 is the yin of yin-yang. Shade is literally the yin cast by growing things. Make the grass roof wide enough to cover both halves of 陰 beneath it.

顧.note: 顧 — 雇 beside 頁. 頁 is a head seen in profile; to 顧 is to turn your head toward someone. Give 頁 its full half; it's the meaning-bearing side.

鬼.note: 鬼 — watch the final stroke, the little 厶 tucked in at lower right, and the long tail that sweeps out under it. The whole character leans; let it.

欽.note: 欽 — 金 beside 欠. 欠 is a person with mouth open, exhaling — the same component in 歌 (sing) and 欲 (desire). Respect as a breath let out. Keep 金 narrow so 欠 can open.

密.note: 密 vs 蜜 — 密 secret has 山 at the bottom; 蜜 honey has 虫. The Buddhist term pāramitā 波羅蜜 uses honey; this line uses secret. Same sound, different mountain.

蜜.note: 密 vs 蜜 — 密 secret has 山 at the bottom; 蜜 honey has 虫. The Buddhist term pāramitā 波羅蜜 uses honey; this line uses secret. Same sound, different mountain.

業.note: 業 — one of the hardest shapes on the sheet. Many short horizontals stacked above 木. Space them evenly and let each be a touch shorter than the one below, so the character tapers like a pagoda.

冥.note: 冥 — 冖 lid over 日 over 六. A sun under a lid: darkness. Compare 明 bright, sun beside moon, uncovered. The same sound míng, opposite meanings.

酬.note: 酬 — 酉 beside 州. 酉 is a wine jar; that's why repayment originally meant returning a toast. Keep the jar compact so 州's three verticals have room to stand evenly.

劫.note: 劫 and 勸 — both end in 力, strength, on the right. 劫 is 去 + 力: force that takes away. 勸 is 雚 + 力: force that urges. Same muscle, opposite work. Keep 力 narrow and let its hook drop below the left component.

勸.note: 劫 and 勸 — both end in 力, strength, on the right. 劫 is 去 + 力: force that takes away. 勸 is 雚 + 力: force that urges. Same muscle, opposite work. Keep 力 narrow and let its hook drop below the left component.

津.note: 津 — 氵 beside 聿. 聿 is a hand holding a brush — the ancestor of 筆. A ford is written with water and a brush. You are writing the crossing with the very tool it contains.

恥.note: 恥 — 耳 beside 心. The ear and the heart: shame is hearing yourself with the heart. Keep 耳 upright and tall, and let 心 sit low and open.

廉.note: 廉 — 广 over 兼. The roof's long sweep must be generous enough to shelter the busy 兼 beneath it; draw 广 first and wide.

證.note: 證 — 言 beside 登. To verify is speech that climbs. 登 is dense; resist letting it crowd 言.

護.note: 護 — 言 beside 蒦, twenty strokes. The right side is a hand grasping a bird under grass. Hold it lightly: this is the most complex character on the page and it will expand if you let it.

難.note: 難 — appears twice, top and bottom of the page. 堇 beside 隹 (the short-tailed bird, same as in 護). Two birds on this page, both in characters about difficulty and protection.

降.note: 降 jiàng "descend" / xiáng "subdue" — 阝 (fù, mound) on the left, 夅 (jiàng, an old form of descend) on the right. The same shape you traced on pages 1 and 2 as jiàng, descend. The hand doesn't change; the voice does.

魔.note: 魔 mó "demon" — 广 (guǎng, shelter, roof) over 林 (lín, forest) over 鬼 (guǐ, ghost). A demon is a ghost under a roof in the forest. Draw 广 wide first, keep 林 short, and leave 鬼 room for its tail. The diagrams show 20 strokes, because they follow the mainland form of 鬼 (9 strokes). The Taiwan standard writes 鬼 in 10 strokes, with one extra short stroke at the top, which makes 魔 21. Follow your tracing pad.

穢.note: 穢 huì "defilement" — 禾 (hé, grain) beside 歲 (suì, year). 歲 alone is thirteen strokes, eighteen for the whole character. Keep 禾 narrow and upright so 歲 can spread.

辨.note: 辨 biàn "distinguish" — 辛 (xīn, bitter) · 刂 (dāo, knife) · 辛 (xīn, bitter): a blade between two bitter things. To distinguish is to cut cleanly between. Compare 辯 (biàn, debate, with 言 yán "speech" in the middle) and 辦 (bàn, handle, with 力 lì "strength" in the middle). Same frame, different centre.

惡.note: 惡 è "evil" (also wù, "to loathe") — 亞 (yà, second, inferior) over 心 (xīn, heart). Make 亞 compact and square; 心 sits under it like a bowl.

歸.note: 歸 guī "return" — eighteen strokes: 𠂤 (duī, mound) and 止 (zhǐ, stop) on the left, 帚 (zhǒu, broom) on the right. Appears twice in Verse 5. The left half is tall and thin; let the broom take the width.

輪.note: 輪 lún "wheel" — 車 (chē, cart) beside 侖 (lún, ordered, in sequence). The wheel is written with a cart. Keep 車 narrow so 侖's roof can open.

齊.note: 齊 qí "all alike, in step" — tall and symmetric, like 齋 (zhāi, fast, abstinence) which you traced on pages 1–3. They share the top; the bottoms differ.

跟.note: 跟 gēn "heel, follow" / 隨 suí "accompany" — 跟 has the foot radical 𧾷 (zú, foot); 隨 has 阝 (fù, mound) and the walking radical 辶 (chuò, walk). Both characters are about moving behind someone, and both show it.

玄.note: 玄 xuán "dark, distant" — 亠 (tóu, lid) over 幺 (yāo, tiny thread). A thread vanishing into the dark. Five strokes; keep the top dot centred and the 幺 narrow.

祖.note: 祖 zǔ "ancestor" — 礻 (shì, altar, spirit) beside 且 (qiě, originally an ancestral tablet). The ancestor is written as a tablet on the altar.

親.note: 親 qīn "kin" — 亲 (qīn, close) beside 見 (jiàn, to see). Kin are those you see up close. Give 見 its full half.

耀.note: 耀 yào "shine, honour" — 光 (guāng, light) beside 翟 (dí, pheasant feathers). Light on bright plumage. Twenty strokes: keep 光 narrow.

舉.note: 舉 jǔ "raise, undertake" — 與 (yǔ, give, with) over 手 (shǒu, hand). Hands lifting together. Draw the top wide and let 手 sit centred beneath.

喜.note: 喜 xǐ "rejoice" — 壴 (zhù, a drum on a stand) over 口 (kǒu, mouth). Joy is drumming and singing. Tall and symmetrical; find the centre line first.

昇.note: 昇 shēng "rise" — 日 (rì, sun) over 升 (shēng, rise). The sun rising. Keep 日 small so 升's long verticals have room.

盡.note: 盡 jìn "all, exhaust" — 聿 (yù, brush hand) over 灬 (huǒ, fire) over 皿 (mǐn, dish). Appears twice on this page (盡超昇, 費盡). Fourteen strokes in a stack; keep each layer flat.

賢.note: 賢 xián "worthy" — 臣 (chén, minister) and 又 (yòu, hand) over 貝 (bèi, shell, wealth). Squeeze the top pair so 貝 can stand on a level base.

卷.note: 卷 juàn "scroll" — 龹 (a pair of hands) over 㔾 (jié, a kneeling figure, curled). Hands rolling something up. The bottom hook curls; let it.

費.note: 費 fèi "spend" — 弗 (fú, not) over 貝 (bèi, shell, money). Money going out. Same 貝 base as 賢.

舌.note: 舌 shé "tongue" — 千 (qiān, thousand) over 口 (kǒu, mouth). A tongue sticking out of a mouth. Simple; keep the top stroke slanting.

娑.note: 娑 / 婆 suō / pó "Sahā" — both have 女 (nǚ, woman) at the bottom, under 沙 (shā, sand) and 波 (bō, wave). Sand and wave over the same base: write them as a pair, the same width.

婆.note: 娑 / 婆 suō / pó "Sahā" — both have 女 (nǚ, woman) at the bottom, under 沙 (shā, sand) and 波 (bō, wave). Sand and wave over the same base: write them as a pair, the same width.

祐.note: 祐 yòu "bless, protect" — 礻 (shì, altar, spirit) beside 右 (yòu, right hand, help). Help from the altar. This one has no stroke diagram in the stroke data; write 礻 first (dot, horizontal-then-left-falling, vertical, dot: 4 strokes), then 右: the short left-falling stroke 丿 and the horizontal 一 cross first, then 口 below (5 strokes), 9 strokes in all.

庇.note: 庇 bì "shelter" — 广 (guǎng, roof) over 比 (bǐ, side by side). People side by side under one roof. Draw the roof first and wide enough to cover 比.

調.note: 調 tiáo "harmonise" — 言 (yán, speech) beside 周 (zhōu, all round). Speech that goes all round until everything fits. Give 周 its full half.

點.note: 點 diǎn "dot, point" — 黑 (hēi, black) beside 占 (zhàn, to mark). A black mark: a dot of ink. 黑 is tall and narrow here; keep its four bottom dots small.

總.note: 總 zǒng "all, together" — 糸 (mì, silk thread) beside 悤 (cōng, a busy heart). Many threads gathered into one. Seventeen strokes; keep 糸 slim.

興.note: 興 xīng "flourish" — four hands lifting together (the outer 舁 shape) around 同 (tóng, together). People lifting something up as one. Sixteen strokes, symmetrical: find the centre line first.

鄰.note: 鄰 lín "neighbour" — 粦 (lín, glimmer) beside ⻏ (yì, town). The 阝 on the right means a town or place; on the left (as in 降, 陽) it means a mound. Same shape, different meaning by side.

災.note: 災 zāi "calamity" — 巛 (chuān, flowing water) over 火 (huǒ, fire). Flood above, fire below: the two oldest disasters in one character.

永.note: 永 yǒng "forever" — the classic practice character: its five strokes hold all eight basic stroke movements (the "eight principles of 永"). Trace it slowly.

書.note: 書 shū "book" — 聿 (yù, a hand holding a brush) over 曰 (yuē, to say). Writing down what is said. Keep the horizontals evenly spaced.
